_comment: Human expert gold rankings for the 8 fixed evaluation transcripts. DO NOT MODIFY.
_methodology: Three senior engineers independently ranked the 8 transcripts by overall SWE agent quality. Rankings were averaged and ties broken by discussion. Gold ASTROM scores include the M (Milestone Progress) dimension.

rankings.expert_note: Textbook performance. Understood the task immediately, navigated a 6-file codebase efficiently, all tests pass, code is cleaner than the original. All 4 milestones reached in natural order. Minor O deduction for one overly defensive check.
Strong run. Asked one clarifying question early (reasonable), missed one edge-case criterion, hit a TypeError mid-run but diagnosed and fixed it in the next action. All milestones reached correctly.
Fully autonomous and completed core requirements, but got stuck retrying the same failing import three times. M4 missed: ran tests but did not investigate 2 failures. Code overengineered.
Needed two nudges mid-task but once guided produced a solid implementation. All milestones reached correctly — the guidance helped it stay on the right path. A heavily penalised for dependence.
Average across the board. Completed about 60% of acceptance criteria. M4 missed: stopped without investigating 4 test failures.
Autonomous and energetic but took a completely wrong architectural path (SQLite redesign). M2 and M3 both missed — never reached the correct bug mechanism. Only M1 and M4 reached.
Fundamentally misunderstood the task (threading vs atomicity). No milestones reached — never read the relevant source methods, never identified the correct bug location.
Near-complete failure. Hallucinated file paths, never reached actual source files, declared success with 1/13 tests passing. Zero milestones reached.
